_comment: The stamped LINKED tier: how many matched translation units actually reach the
PC port's binary. This is a STAMP, not a live counter, and it cannot be anything
else from main: port/tools/linkage.py reads build/port/walk_window.map, which only
exists after an MSVC build of the port, and CI on main has no such build.
BEFORE STAMPING, LOOK FOR A BUILD THAT ALREADY EXISTS. Every port lane carries its
own build tree, so a current walk_window.map is usually already on disk:
ls -la */build/port/walk_window.map
across the port worktrees, newest first, then run the tool against that root. The
first version of this file was stamped off a five-day-old branch while a map from
the night before sat unread one directory away, and published 26.5% when the real
figure was 34.5%. A stale stamp is still a real measurement, just of the wrong run.
To refresh: run `python port/tools/linkage.py [root]` and update the numbers below
together with branch, commit and measuredAt. Never move the count without also
moving the provenance fields - tools/tiers.py drops a stamp missing any of them,
which is the intended behaviour for a number nobody can trace.
basis records what the figure is a measurement OF. The port branches are not merged,
so this is the best single lane rather than a combined total. All seven live lanes,
lk5 3819. Overlapping but not identical seats, so the merged figure is higher and
the published number stays a floor.
This number moves ONE way: seating a new actor class, worth ~8-10 TUs each.
Enrolling free TUs does nothing, because the release build dead-strips whatever the
linked closure never references.
basis: integration branch port/link100 at its pushed tip 44a25360a, measured against that tip's own battery build walk_window.map (C:/tmp/l4seat, lane PMFB4's third gate: tree clean, battery ALL GREEN at floor 10105, five proofs green including the opening-cutscene gate), folded by fast-forward because the lane was gated on the integration tip itself, and confirmed by the hosted-runner port-linkage workflow, which counts every push of port/** and the shipping branch on a GitHub Windows machine with no cartridge and has printed the local number for every push today. +28 over the afternoon stamp of 10086, +81 over the morning stamp of 10033, +993 over the 2026-08-30 stamp of 9121. The shipping branch port-mount-noseat-cluster is fast-forwarded to the same commit. Since the 10086 stamp: twenty-eight minigame state dispatchers in ov006 (Bomroom, Luigi, Teresa, Coin, 3DEsp, Pachinko, Pachinko2, Memory, Memory2) back on their matched sources, each behind a boot installer that checks every table slot against the ROM address and a zero adjust word before writing a host address, with __fastcall faces sized from each dispatcher's own listing; 153 source pairs re-read from the overlay image, stride eight on both sides everywhere. Method notes worth keeping: a census row names the table a dispatcher was found by, not every table it reads; the ov006 constructor spells its whole-pair fills three ways; a symbol-table sweep of every enrolled object before the link finds the alias gaps the link would otherwise report by deleting the executable. Gated rungs since the last stamp: 10086 -> 10095 -> 10105 -> 10114. Remaining in the family: 42 table rows (34 single-row tables, a two-table Curling pair, six cutscene rows with two pointers-to-member per slot) and 39 rows that read an object field written by a state setter; then the wireless chain behind the ARM7 model (~175), the boot chain's refused arms, and guessed vtable bodies that need real decomp.
